# Physiology, Tooth

**Authors:** Barret Zimmerman, Karlie R. Shumway, Andrew C. Jenzer

**Source:** StatPearls - StatPearls Publishing

## Abstract

Teeth serve multiple functions beyond mastication, including shaping the kinetics of phonation, breathing, maintaining a patent airway, and serving as a foundation for the vertical dimensions of the face. The maxilla and mandible, which together form the jaw, contain alveolar bone, a thick ridge of bone that forms the sockets of the teeth. Appropriate size and jaw positioning are critical in developing a proper bite (occlusion) and subsequent mastication. As discussed later in detail, certain teeth have specialized roles in chewing, with the entire group functioning as a dynamic entity.
